Thalvik
Seed round — Confidential

Spend management that closes the books before the month does.

Thalvik gives mid-market finance teams a single card-and-invoice layer that
reconciles itself, so controllers stop spending the first eight working days
of every month chasing receipts and coding lines in a spreadsheet.

Copenhagen, Denmark. Founded 2024. 11 people.
Raising a EUR 3.5M seed round.

The problem

Mid-market companies (150-1,500 employees) run spend on three disconnected
systems: corporate cards issued by their bank, invoices arriving as PDFs in a
shared mailbox, and an ERP that only learns about either one at month-end.

What that costs, from 40 discovery interviews with Nordic and German
controllers between March and September 2025:

- 6 to 9 working days of every month are spent on reconciliation and receipt
  chasing. Controllers we spoke to described it as "the part of the job nobody
  put in the job description."
- 18% of card transactions in the median company we looked at are still
  missing a receipt 30 days after the purchase.
- Policy is enforced after the money is gone. Three of the 40 companies had
  discovered duplicate subscription spend above EUR 100k only at audit.
- The average controller in our sample maintains 2 shadow spreadsheets that
  exist purely to bridge the card statement and the ERP.

Finance leaders do not describe this as a software problem. They describe it as
a staffing problem, and they solve it by hiring another accountant.

Our solution

Thalvik replaces the card, the invoice inbox and the coding step with one
ledger-aware layer.

1. Issue virtual and physical cards with policy attached at issuance, not
   reviewed afterwards. A card can be scoped to one vendor, one budget line
   and one date range.
2. Capture the receipt at the moment of purchase. Our mobile prompt fires on
   the authorisation, not on the settled transaction, so the employee is
   still standing at the counter.
3. Code the line automatically. Thalvik reads the vendor, the historical
   coding pattern for that vendor in that company, and the budget owner, and
   proposes the ledger account and cost centre. The controller approves in
   bulk or overrides.
4. Push to the ERP continuously. We write to the general ledger daily rather
   than in a month-end batch, so the close is a review, not a reconstruction.

The wedge is step 3. Card issuance is commoditised. Continuous, company-
specific coding that a controller actually trusts is not.

Product and how it works

Live today:
- Virtual and physical card issuance via our BIN sponsor (a licensed EMI in
  Lithuania). Multi-currency in EUR, DKK, SEK, NOK.
- Receipt capture (iOS, Android, email forwarding, WhatsApp).
- Invoice ingestion with line-item extraction, PO matching where a PO exists.
- Coding engine: per-tenant model trained on that tenant's first 90 days of
  approved codings, with a confidence score surfaced to the controller. We do
  not auto-post anything below 0.9 confidence.
- Native integrations: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, e-conomic,
  Fortnox, Xero. NetSuite is in private beta with two customers.
- Approval workflows, budget-owner notifications, spend policy engine.

In build for Q1-Q2 2026:
- Accounts payable: scheduled vendor payments from the Thalvik balance.
- Multi-entity consolidation (the top request from our four largest accounts).
- SOC 2 Type II (audit window opens February 2026).

Not built and deliberately out of scope: payroll, procurement sourcing,
treasury, and anything requiring us to hold a banking licence ourselves.

Market

TAM — USD 48B. Global spend management and B2B expense software, all company
sizes, 2025. We take Gartner's enterprise-software category revenue for
"travel and expense plus procure-to-pay" and add the card interchange pool
attributable to commercial cards issued by fintechs.

SAM — USD 6.2B. Companies of 150-1,500 employees in the Nordics, DACH and
Benelux. Roughly 61,000 companies at a blended USD 102k annual contract value
across software and interchange.

SOM — USD 2.9B within three years. We expect Thalvik to reach 2.9B of
annualised revenue and interchange across the SAM by the end of year three on
the back of accountant-channel distribution, which compounds faster than
direct sales in this segment.

Why the market is opening now:
- PSD2 and the Nordic open-banking rails make ledger-grade transaction data
  available without a bank partnership.
- E-invoicing mandates (Germany from 2025, Belgium from 2026) force every
  company in the SAM to touch their AP stack in the next 24 months.
- Mid-market finance headcount has been flat while transaction volume per
  company has grown, so the buyer now has a budget line for automation.

Competition

Thalvik sits between three groups, none of which solves the mid-market
coding problem.

SAP Concur — the incumbent. Strong at enterprise travel policy and global
compliance. Implementation runs 6-9 months and starts around EUR 60k, which
prices out everyone under 1,500 employees. No card issuance of its own, no
continuous ledger write-back. We win on time-to-value.

Legacy ERP add-on modules (Dynamics expense modules, Fortnox add-ons) — cheap
and already in the stack, but they are forms over a database. No card, no
capture at authorisation, no coding intelligence. We win on the actual work.

Spreadsheets and the shared invoice mailbox — still our most common
competitor, present in 26 of our 34 paying customers before they bought
Thalvik. We win because the controller's own time is the budget.

Why now, why us: we are the only team combining a controller who has closed
books in this exact segment with an engineering team that has shipped card
issuing at scale. Everyone else is attacking either the card or the ledger,
never the seam between them.

Traction

Revenue:
- EUR 41,300 MRR as of 30 November 2025 (software subscription only;
  interchange is reported separately below).
- EUR 9,100 of monthly interchange revenue on EUR 2.3M of monthly card volume.
- 11% average month-over-month MRR growth across the last six months.

Customers:
- 34 paying customers. Median 240 employees.
- Largest account: EUR 4,100 MRR, a Danish facilities-services group.
- 6 signed letters of intent from accounting firms who would resell Thalvik to
  their own client base (approximately 900 companies behind those six firms).

Engagement and retention:
- 71% weekly active rate among licensed seats.
- 4.1% monthly logo churn. Three of the six churned accounts cited the
  missing multi-entity consolidation.
- Net revenue retention 106% over the last two quarters.
- Median close time at our customers fell from 9.5 days to 4.0 days after two
  full months on Thalvik (self-reported by the controller).

Efficiency:
- Blended CAC EUR 3,850. Payback 9.5 months.
- Sales team of one (the CEO). All 34 customers closed founder-led.

Business model

Two revenue lines.

1. Subscription. EUR 14 per active employee per month, billed annually, with a
   EUR 490 monthly platform floor. Median contract today is EUR 1,215 MRR.
   No implementation fee — onboarding is 8 working days, done by our own
   customer-success engineer.

2. Interchange. We keep 0.40% of card volume net of scheme and BIN-sponsor
   fees. At current volumes this is 18% of revenue; we model it settling
   around 25-30% as card adoption inside accounts matures.

Unit economics at the median account:
- Gross margin 74% on subscription, 61% blended including interchange and
  BIN-sponsor cost.
- Support cost EUR 62 per account per month.

Pricing power: the buyer compares us to the loaded cost of half an accountant
(EUR 2,600/month in Denmark), not to other software. That framing has let us
raise list price twice in 14 months with no measurable close-rate impact.

Go to market: founder-led direct into 150-600 employee companies, and the
accountant channel as the scale motion from Q2 2026.

Team

Mikkel Ravnsborg — CEO. Spent six years at A.P. Moller - Maersk in group
finance, where he ran the monthly close for the terminals division and led the
rollout of a spend-policy programme across 14 country entities. Left as Head
of Finance Operations. Copenhagen Business School, MSc Finance and Accounting.
He is the controller we are building for.

Aino Lehtinen — CTO. Nine years in payments engineering, most recently four
years at Klarna where she was a staff engineer on the card-issuing platform
and, in her final year, tech lead for the merchant settlement service. Before
that, backend infrastructure at a Helsinki logistics scale-up. Aalto
University, MSc Computer Science.

The two met in 2021 while Mikkel's team was evaluating card programmes and
Aino's team was the vendor. They incorporated Thalvik in April 2024 after nine
months of nights-and-weekends prototyping.

Team: 11 people. 6 engineers, 2 customer success, 1 designer, plus the
founders. Two of the engineers followed Aino from her previous company.

Advisors: a former CFO of a listed Nordic industrials group, and a partner at
a Copenhagen accounting firm who introduced our first four customers.

The ask

Raising EUR 3.5M seed on a EUR 18M pre-money valuation. EUR 1.2M is soft-
circled from two Nordic funds; we are looking for a lead for the remainder.

Use of funds over 22 months of runway:
- 45% engineering (8 hires: AP payments, multi-entity, NetSuite, and the
  coding model).
- 30% go-to-market (2 account executives, 1 partner manager for the
  accountant channel, and the channel programme itself).
- 15% compliance and licensing. We have applied for our own EMI licence in
  Denmark to replace the BIN-sponsor arrangement; the application went in in
  October 2025 and we assume approval within 12 months.
- 10% general and administrative.

Milestones we are underwriting to:
- EUR 250k MRR by month 18.
- 40 accounting-firm partners live, contributing 50% of new logos.
- SOC 2 Type II and the EMI licence in hand.

Cap table today: founders 71% (Mikkel 38%, Aino 33%), employee option pool 9%
(6% granted), pre-seed angels 8%, and 12% held in common stock by our first
advisor from a 2024 arrangement made before we had counsel.
